subject: HONR
disclaimer: NU Map is an independent, student-built planner. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or officially connected to Northeastern University. Data is scraped from Northeastern's public catalog and refreshed on a schedule; always confirm with the official catalog and an academic advisor.

legend.prereqs: Flat token list: course refs {subject, number, minGrade} joined by 'And'/'Or' strings; nested arrays are parenthesized groups. minGrade is the minimum passing grade required.
legend.coreqs: Courses that must be taken in the same term.
legend.offerings.terms: Past/scheduled terms by Banner code (YYYY = academic-year END year; Fall runs in YYYY-1). sections/enrolled/capacity are snapshots from the scheduled scrape, NOT live seat availability.
legend.offerings.typicalDays: Weekdays on which at least 50% of recent sections met.
legend.offerings.daysPct: Percent of recent sections meeting on each weekday (M/T/W/Th/F).
legend.offerings.meetingPatterns: [pattern, percent-of-sections] pairs; in patterns like 'MWR', R means Thursday.
legend.instructors: Per season. sharePct = average percent of that season's enrolled students taught by this professor (recent terms). 'reviews' links their RateMyHusky page when one exists.
legend.level: undergrad for course numbers below 5000, grad otherwise.
legend.typicallyOffered: Seasons in which the course was scheduled in at least two-thirds of that season's terms on record since it first appeared — a pattern, not a guarantee.
legend.unlocks: Courses that list this course in their prerequisites — what taking it opens up.
legend.nuPath: NUpath general-education attributes this course carries.
legend.repeatable: Whether the course may be taken more than once for credit (repeatMax / repeatMaxSH cap it).

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Discovery
courses.description: Offers students an opportunity to take full advantage of the John Martinson Honors Program and to foster a sense of community within the first-year honors experience. Students explore the goals of the program through a variety of experiential learning activities such as taking part in a theme-based living/learning community, learning through an interdisciplinary perspective, advancing their global mindset, and making an impact in the communities that they inhabit. Required for all first-year honors students.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Inquiry
courses.description: Designed to provide an honors introductory-level experience. Draws upon an interdisciplinary perspective to expand individual knowledge and facilitate a deeper understanding of issues. Similar to a topics course, each section of the course offers a new and unique academic experience. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Research and Creative Endeavors in Honors
courses.description: Offers University Honors students an opportunity to conduct research and creative endeavors under faculty supervision. Requires the permission of instructor and University Honors Program. May be repeated two times for a maximum of 12 semester hours.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Research and Creative Endeavors
courses.description: Offers an opportunity to document student contributions to research projects or creative endeavors performed under faculty supervision. Requires the permission of instructor and University Honors Program. May be repeated nine times.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar Abroad
courses.description: Seeks to promote knowledge, understanding, and global engagement through course work, language acquisition, travel, and participation in a Northeastern University designed and delivered international academic experience. Targeted toward honors students who may not have the opportunity to complete international work later on in their academic career or who want to have an early international experience prior to a more traditional study abroad or international co-op experience. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Seminar
courses.description: Designed to provide an honors intermediate-level experience. Draws upon an interdisciplinary perspective to expand individual knowledge and facilitate a more advanced understanding of issues. Emphasizes research and inquiry of urban, historical, or contemporary themes. May be repeated up to nine times.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Directed Study
courses.description: Offers independent work under the direction of the department on a chosen topic. Course content depends on instructor. Requires Honors Program participation. May be repeated without limit.

courses.subject: HONR
courses.title: Honors Interdisciplinary Thesis
courses.description: Represents a culmination of the diverse topics students encounter while enrolled in the University Honors Program. Offers students an opportunity to work closely with a faculty mentor to conduct intensive original research that includes an interdisciplinary perspective and produces a significant body of work. The thesis should utilize a cross-discipline perspective that includes at least two disciplines, allowing students to express their academic creativity, to discover new ways of synthesizing information, and to test the traditional boundaries between disciplines.
